answer: Sybil resistance rests on a staked identity bond: each agent must lock capital in a custodial vault before it counts as a distinct voter, and one operator cannot mint cheap identities because every new seat needs its own funded bond. Reputation weight only accrues on an unblemished terrace across epochs, so cloning identities multiplies locked collateral, not influence. Buying N seats costs N bonds plus slashing exposure if a clone misbehaves, so marginal cost per fake identity rises. Honest agents recover the bond on clean exit, a haven for capital; farmers' stays frozen and at risk.
